SUBJECT:  DIRECTOR AND RECREATION MANAGER REPORT

BACKGROUND

The Community Services Director and Recreation Manager provide a monthly report to the
Recreation Commission. The report provides relevant administrative, operational, and financial
updates, as well as information on upcoming events, marketing and communication efforts, and
customer feedback.

DISCUSSION

Community Services Department / Recreation Division Overview Presentation

San Marino Center Update
Provided by Community Services Department (CSD) Council Liaison Ken Ude

Personnel Updates
  • Throughout August and September, we’ve transitioned from our summer programming and
  events into our Fall activities. With that comes the need to bid a fond farewell (until next
  summer) to our 18 PT (part-time) seasonal staff that supported our Aquatics and Summer
  Camp programs. Many of our permanent PT staff from our early childhood program also
  worked as site supervisors at Camp Lacy and Freewheelers.
  • We recently congratulated one of our long-standing Maintenance Assistants, Dale
  DeGuzman, who was promoted internally (after 7 years working part-time) to the Parks and
  Public Works (PPW) Department as a full-time Maintenance Worker I.
  • We recently welcomed Jonathon Morataya as a new Maintenance Assistant. You will often
  see him performing room set-ups and take-downs, assisting with event logistics, and
  supporting audio/video productions for a variety of public meeting in the Barth Room at the
  Crowell Public Library (CPL).

  Page 4 of 11
 NEW Home for the Holidays Event – December 9
Planning is well underway for the City’s newest event. It was recently introduced in the Fall
Community Services Guide on pages 4 and 9. As many may recall, this event replaces the former
“Christmas Around the Drive” event that was managed by the local Chamber group for many years.
The City Council approved $60,000 to have the City/CSD take over this event, as well as refurbish
the Holiday House Bus Shelter located on San Marino Avenue and Huntington Drive.

Lacy Park Gatehouse Transition from PPW to CSD
Last spring, it was decided that CSD would assume oversight of Gatehouse operations at the main
entrance of Lacy Park. CSD is better suited to support consistent staffing and managerial
responsibilities of this year-round, weekend operation. Open only on the weekends to capture non-
resident user fees, the Recreation Division PT staff will not only provide customer service to patrons
entering and leaving the park, but will also serve as a point of contact for rental customers. Lastly,
as part of the transition, CSD is thrilled to be working in partnership with the PPW Department to
install a new, pre-fabricated gatehouse, computer/POS system, and improved signage. Installation of
the new mini-structure will occur sometime in mid to late September or early October.

Mark Your Calendar for Literary Libations – October 15
Please consider attending the San Marino Public Library Foundation’s fall fundraiser event on
Saturday, October 15 at the Crowell Public Library from 6 – 9 PM. This ticketed event features an
evening of delectable food and wine tastings, a variety of beers and whiskeys, and literary activities
spaced throughout the book stacks. All net proceeds benefit future capital improvements, as well as
advancing technology infrastructure at CPL. For details, please visit sanmarinoplf.org.

Operational Staff Briefings
  Aquatics
  For the 2022 summer aquatics season, the Recreation Division transitioned from a third
  party aquatics management company back to providing an in-house aquatics program. A 9-
  week facility use agreement was entered into with San Marino Unified School District for
  the use of the High School pool from May 31 – July 31. Recreation Manager Covarrubias
  successfully recruited a lifeguard team of 14, which included two supervisors that oversaw
  daily operations. Total number of participants during the 9-week program was 2,185: group
  lessons (282), private lessons (101), Open Swim (1,048), Water Walking (87), summer camp
  swimmers (667). There were no major accidents or incidents. Customer satisfaction surveys
  were conducted throughout the season and staff are pleased to report an overall satisfaction
  rating of 4.80 out of 5.

  Summer Camps
  Camp Lacy served 428 youth ranging in age from 5 – 14. Ten weeks of day camp was offered
  in the following programs: Jr. Adventurers and Trailblazers, Freewheelers, Jr. TITAN Sports
  Camp, and a Counselor in Training (CIT) program. Campers participated in arts and crafts,
  games, field trips, trips to the pool, nature walks, and more! A highlight for many of the
  campers was going to Buena Park to attend The Pirates Dinner Adventure show. Would-be
  pirates of all ages took part in the epic interactive dinner show. Customer satisfaction surveys
  were conducted at the end of the season and staff are pleased to report an overall satisfaction
  rating of 4.72 out of 5.

  Summer Sunset Concert Series
  The Recreation Division successfully hosted its second annual Summer Sunset Concert
  Series at Lacy Park. The dates of the concerts were July 22, August 5, and August 19. The
  three bands that performed were: Neon Nation, playing a wide variety of popular 80’s hits;
  Hot August Night, a tribute band to the legendary Neil Diamond; and The Kings of 88,
  blasting sing along rock-piano anthems. Attendance was estimated between 1,800-2,200 for
  the entire concert series. The setting of the concerts and the time of day made for a perfect
  atmosphere for families and friends to dance and sing together.

  Page 6 of 11
   Contract Classes
  The City of San Marino has developed a program selection that best meets the needs of local
  residents and introduced new and diversified classes for increased community participation.
  This summer, a variety of options were offered including cooking, STEM, and performing arts
  classes. This summer, 455 people partook in these specialized offerings. One highlight was
  the resurgence of line dancing for adults taught by instructor Waylie Tang. Over 30
  participants registered to take the class in its first offering since the pandemic began.

  Senior Happy Hour
  A free Backyard BBQ themed event was held for San Marino residents ages 55 and older at
  Lacy Park on July 20. 65 participants enjoyed a delicious BBQ dinner, dessert, and cold drinks.
  Entertainment was provided by Cowgirl Christy Lewis who thrilled the crowd with western
  roping tricks and a bullwhip demonstration, and taught guests how to country line dance.
  The Happy Hour series is funded by the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG)
  Senior Outreach.

Commendations / Customer Feedback
  Happy Hour
  - Fun times with old neighbors and new! Thanks for organizing a terrific event. This

  who are so lonesome most times.

  Aquatics
  - It has been a really positive experience and everyone we have worked with has
  been really helpful.
  - Bella is fantastic with children. ALL of the staff are friendly and welcoming. This is
  a gem of a program.
  - Instructor and manager worked with our kids a great deal to ensure a great,
  positive, successful learning experience!
  - Great energy and personality from all staff. Very helpful.
  - The swim program at San Marino High School is the best kept secret in San
  Marino. The classes are well run and the instructors are fun and playful with the
  kids. The supervisor (whose name escapes me) is always present, supervising the
  younger staff members, greeting children and adults, and welcoming everyone. I
  could not have been happier or more delighted with the swim lessons. Thank you
  so much and I look forward to next summer!!

  Camp Lacy
  - Our son enjoyed the week fully. He had a blast at the field trip as well. Trip to
  Magic Mountain was extremely fun.
  - Enjoyed Lost World laser tag!
  - Water park was a huge success!

 SUBJECT:  4TH OF JULY EVENT RECAP

BACKGROUND

Since 1965, the City of San Marino has been celebrating the 4th of July holiday with a community
parade, picnic, and fireworks show at Lacy Park. Several key civic groups, such as The Chamber of
Commerce, Rotary Club, and City Club, have played an integral role in keeping this beloved
community tradition alive. Since 2006, the Recreation Division has been spearheading the event-day
activities inside the Park, including the fireworks show. Rotary Club has managed the community
parade for many years, and City Club has been hosting The Pavilion since 2014.

5-Year Attendance Estimates
For a community with a population of approximately 13K, to successfully host a one-day event that
averages around 9K attendees is quite an impressive accomplishment. From a historic perspective,
the community has continued to enjoy and support this beloved event for 57 years!

  2017  2018  2019  2021  2022
  9,632  9,399  9,159  6,169  8,694
NOTE: 2020 no event due to the pandemic.

5-Year Budget Actuals
  2017  2018  2019  2021  2022

 Revenue  $  60,020  $ 56,580  $ 61,175  $  42,785  $  64,570

 *Expense  $  80,501  $ 62,483  $ 63,870  $  82,320  $  84,823

 Net / (GF Support)  $ (20,481)  $ (5,903)  $ (2,695)  $ (39,535)  $ (20,253)

 ** % Cost Recovery  74%  91%  96%  52%  76%
NOTE: * Includes direct expenses and all FT/PT personnel day of event expenses.
  ** Average % of cost recovery for events with mostly a community benefit is 0 - 25%. Source – NPRA & GreenPlayLLC.

  Page 9 of 11
 DISCUSSION

Event Highlights
With the pandemic waning, attendance this year bounced back to near historical levels. The
reoccurring sentiment from the community was that everyone was thrilled to be back in-person
enjoying San Marino’s quintessential summer event at Lacy Park. Led by the Recreation Division, the
interdepartmental Event Committee and Community Partners worked diligently to bring back all of
the crowd-favorite activities – J.P. Blecksmith Memorial Run, Family Fun Zone, Rotary Parade, City
Club Pavilion, main stage entertainment, food vendors, and the fireworks show.

Event Accomplishments – What Went Well
The Event Committee not only focused on restoring the event to its full glory post-pandemic, but
they were pleased to have made some key operational improvements: enhanced public messaging
related to event parking, added new event-day signage and site map display, improved the event
brochure – content and design, began Committee planning meetings two months earlier, and utilized
new registration software to manage wristband sales. Community Partners (City Club and Rotary
Club) praised city staff for their professionalism and helpfulness; they believed both the Parade and
Pavilion operations were well received by spectators and participants. City Club reported that
tickets were in high demand. Rotary Club shared that while entries were slow to be received,
volunteer support and community patriotism was wonderful.

Event Challenges – What Didn’t Go Well
Post-event debrief meetings were recently held by the Event Committee, the City’s Executive Team,
as well as with our Community Partners (City Club and Rotary Club). Various operational concerns
and challenges were brought forward throughout these collaborative meetings. The areas creating
the most concern were: 1) High attendance continues to impact neighborhood parking, creating
potentially unsafe conditions for attendees entering and leaving the park; 2) Event security concerns
were raised related to current staffing levels and the ability to provide adequate security at both
entrance points, side exit gates, as well as throughout the Park; 3) Staff observed patrons not
adhering to Park and Event Guidelines related to the prohibition of intoxicating beverages and
controlled substances; 4) Concerns were shared about fencing quality and visibility (lighting) when
exiting the Park after the fireworks show; 5) Challenges were experienced with Community Partners
getting their event permit paperwork submitted in a timely manner and/or upholding permit
responsibilities. City Club reported that the Pavilion budget struggles to breakeven, and securing
volunteers gets more difficult each year. Rotary Club shared that lack of signage and barricades
hindered the clearance of the Parade route.

Looking Ahead
Upon receipt of feedback from the Recreation Commission today and City Council on September
30, Staff will provide viable solutions and recommendations that address safety and liability issues
for Council’s consideration. This report will be given after the first of the year.

  Page 10 of 11
 RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends the Commission receive and file the 4th of July Event Recap and provide voluntary
feedback. Upon providing comments and/or feedback, an appropriate motion would be:

“I move to receive and file the 4th of July Recap.”
